key_insight: ARDY aims to combine the best of both worlds: the control and quality of offline motion generation with the speed needed for interactive, real-time use. It does this through an autoregressive diffusion design and a hybrid motion representation that better preserves long-horizon intent and semantic guidance.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of generating realistic 3D human motion in real time for interactive applications. Existing offline methods are too slow for live use, while existing online methods often lose controllability, struggle with complex text instructions, or fail on long-term motion goals.
method: Uses an autoregressive diffusion framework to generate motion step-by-step while maintaining temporal consistency.
Introduces a hybrid representation to balance fine-grained motion detail with efficient real-time inference.
Targets interactive generation by improving responsiveness to text and kinematic constraints without sacrificing motion realism.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work points toward motion generation systems that are both controllable and deployable in real-time environments. That makes it relevant for animation tools, simulation pipelines, and humanoid robotics where latency and coherence both matter.

paper_title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
paper_authors: Kaifeng Zhao, Mathis Petrovich, Haotian Zhang, Tingwu Wang, Siyu Tang
